title: Gary Gibbs: Sooner Linebacker Who Became OU's Head Coach
question: Which former OU linebacker later became Oklahoma's head coach and then an NFL assistant?
answer: Gary Gibbs, a Sooner linebacker from 1972 to 1974, spent 23 years at OU as a player and coach, led the program from 1989 to 1994, and later coached in the NFL.
summary: Gary Gibbs played linebacker at Oklahoma in 1972-74, ran the Sooners defense, went 44-23-2 as head coach, then coached for the Cowboys, Saints and Chiefs.
body: Gary Gibbs is one of the few men to see Oklahoma football from every chair. A native of Beaumont, Texas, he played linebacker for the Sooners from 1972 to 1974 and earned both his bachelor's and master's degrees at OU.

He never really left. Gibbs began coaching in Norman in 1975 as a graduate assistant, worked up to linebackers coach in 1978, and became defensive coordinator in 1981. He held that job when Barry Switzer's Sooners won the 1985 national championship. In all, he logged 23 years at OU as a player, assistant and head coach.

When Switzer stepped down in 1989, Gibbs took over the program and led it through 1994. His Oklahoma teams went 44-23-2 and reached three bowl games, with the first two seasons of his tenure falling under NCAA postseason sanctions.

After Norman, Gibbs spent 2000 as Georgia's defensive coordinator and 2001 in the same role at LSU under Nick Saban. He then moved to the NFL as Dallas Cowboys linebackers coach, working alongside Sean Payton, and followed Payton to New Orleans as the Saints' defensive coordinator for the 2006 through 2008 seasons.
Pro Football Archives lists him as the Kansas City Chiefs' linebackers coach from 2009 through 2017, a long NFL second act for a former Sooner who had once run his alma mater's program.
